## Seam taxonomy (what the conflicts actually are)

1. **Include-union** (e.g. Canary adds `spirv_compatibility.h`): trivial, take both.
2. **Localized** (1-4 conflicts, a few lines): quick manual review.
3. **Stale cherry-pick** (the real work): ReXGlue pulled a Canary feature early;
   Canary later refactored it, so your copy and Canary's current form both differ
   from base -> conflict. Example: `spirv_translator_rb.cpp` alpha-to-coverage
   (Canary dropped the `fsi_` naming and moved a 187-line block). Resolve by
   re-deriving from Canary's current form, discarding the stale copy.

## PM4 command-processor decision (analyzed)

**Verdict: adopt Canary's PM4 mixin.** Do it last, by *wholesale replacement +
seam re-bridging*, NOT 3-way merge.

Canary's pattern (`pm4_command_processor_declare.h` injected into each class body,
`pm4_command_processor_implement.h` `#include`d into each backend `.cc`) compiles
the PM4 dispatch separately per backend so the hot packet loop inlines and
devirtualizes `IssueDraw`/`WriteRegister`/etc. Master (ReXGlue today) has them as
plain virtuals: one compile, an indirect call per packet.

Why the 57/41/34 conflicts don't 3-way-merge: the handler *signatures differ*.
ReXGlue threads a `memory::RingBuffer* reader` through every handler; Canary made
the reader member state (`GetCurrentRingReadCount()`), which is what enables the
inlining. That's an architecture change, not a line conflict.

Why adopt anyway: (1) ReXGlue is a native-perf runtime -- a devirtualized/inlined
hot loop is on-philosophy and measurably faster on the single hottest GPU path;
(2) it's the only way to ever converge the 132-conflict command-processor cluster
-- staying virtual = re-porting these 3 files by hand forever.

Bridge checklist (bounded; ReXGlue's own divergence here is ~525 lines but only
~62 touch real seams):
- [ ] Add `XE_RESTRICT/NOINLINE/FORCEINLINE/COLD/NOALIAS` equivalents (ReXGlue has
      only `REX_RESTRICT_VAR`) -- add to `rex/platform.h` or map `XE_*`->`REX_*` in rexform.
- [ ] Adopt Canary's implicit member-reader model (drop the `RingBuffer* reader` param).
- [ ] Re-bridge ~3 handlers to ReXGlue's seams: `ExecutePacketType3_INTERRUPT` /
      `_XE_SWAP` -> `graphics_system_->DispatchInterruptCallback` + VdSwap hook;
      thread creation via `system::XHostThread` + `kernel_state_`.
- [ ] Keep ReXGlue's `FunctionDispatcher`, plugin-ABI, `readback_resolve`, null-guards.
- [ ] Method: `ReX_current - base_master` on these files = ReXGlue's seam-bridge set;
      re-apply that set onto rexform'd Canary, rather than merging.

  the backends that populate them.
- **ZPD fragment-shader-interlock** occlusion feature (`buffer_zpd_fsi_counter_` etc.).
- glslang enum differences (`spv::BuiltIn::PrimitiveId`/`VertexIndex`).
Requires syncing the shader **headers** + shared `SystemConstants` + backend populators
together — a feature port (like ZPD in PM4), not a `.cpp`-only merge. NOTE: the worksheet

## APPROACH PIVOT: pour files 1:1 + one translation layer (not 3-way merge)

3-way merging Canary onto ReXGlue's *diverged* fork was the source of every conflict,
stale-cherry-pick, duplicate member, and the SystemConstants "feature port". Proven
empirically: replacing a backend file 1:1 with Canary collapsed a whole feature port to
one wrong include. **New method: treat Canary as source-of-truth, pour files ~1:1 through
rexform, and keep all divergence in ONE translation layer.**

The translation layer (build-once, then files pour in):
- **rexform** — `xe::gpu`->`rex::graphics`, include remap (+ base-header renames:
  `byte_order`->`types`, `profiling`->`dbg`, `xxhash`->`hash`, `string_buffer`->`string/buffer`),
  `cvars::X`->`REXCVAR_GET(X)`, and auto-injects `xe_compat.h`.
- **`include/rex/graphics/xe_compat.h`** — `namespace xe` aliases over `rex::` (bit ops,
  `countof`, `Memory` + endian load/store, `StringBuffer`, `threading`->`thread`,
  `filesystem`), pulled into `rex::graphics` via `using namespace xe`; plus Xenia
  `DEFINE_*`/`DECLARE_*` cvar macros (which reorder desc/category to ReXGlue's), and the
  `XE_*`/`XELOG*` macros via gpu_attributes.h.
- **`spirv_compatibility.h`** — self-protecting (pulls glslang before its macros).
- glslang 16 (keystone).

**Pour granularity is the SUBSYSTEM, not the file** — mixing poured-Canary and diverged
files in one subsystem creates signature/const mismatches (e.g. `StoreResult` arity,
`SystemConstants`). Poured so far (build-verified clean): the full shader subsystem
(translators + base + interpreter + dxbc + spirv), `vulkan/pipeline_cache`,
`vulkan/render_target_cache`.

Remaining to green: (1) a few residual compat gaps as new files pour (add aliases to
xe_compat); (2) `ac6_ground_fix` etc. cvar DECLAREs into `flags.h`; (3) Canary's precompiled
shader bytecode (a build step, not code); (4) the ONE boundary file `vulkan/command_processor`
+ core `command_processor` -- these mix Canary GPU logic with ReXGlue's native-driving seams
(PM4 mixin, FunctionDispatcher, interrupt/swap) and are the only hand-reconciliation.

## KEY FINDING: the real blocker is the base/support layer, not the GPU code

Across PM4, shader, and util, the GPU `.cc`/`.h` merges themselves are tractable —
what blocks each subsystem is Canary's GPU code depending on **newer Canary base/support
APIs that ReXGlue rebased onto `rex::` equivalents and never updated**. Recurring blockers:

| Canary base dependency                    | ReXGlue status         | Blocked |
|-------------------------------------------|------------------------|---------|
| base math: `roundToNearestOrderOfMagnitude`, `ArchReciprocalRefined`, `divisors::MagicDiv` | **ported to `rex/math.h`** | resolved |
| `texture_address::` (tiled addressing)    | **ported: `pipeline/texture/address.h`** | resolved |
| `FormatInfo::GetName`                      | **added (uses existing `name`)** | resolved |
| `XE_*` attr macros, `XE_MAYBE_UNUSED`, `XE_MSVC_OPTIMIZE_*`, `XELOG*` | **added (gpu_attributes.h)** | resolved |
| `swcache::` prefetch + `RingBuffer::BeginPrefetchedRead` | absent | PM4 (stubbed) |
| `logging::LoggerBatch<LogLevel>`          | absent (REXGPU_* only) | PM4 disasm (stubbed) |
| shared `SystemConstants` new members + ZPD-FSI | old struct | SPIRV translators |
| glslang scoped enums (`spv::Op::`, `spvUtil.h`, `spirv.hpp11`) | pre-migration glslang | SPIRV (shimmed inert) |

### draw_util coupling (found while porting the base layer)
Even with all its base-layer deps resolved, `draw_util` **cannot land alone**: its
`ResolveInfo` / `ResolveCopyShaderInfo` structs are consumed by
`vulkan/render_target_cache.cpp` and `vulkan/command_processor.cpp`. Canary's struct
changes (e.g. removing `dest_bpe_log2`, adding `GetResolveDownscalePixelSizeLog2`) break
those consumers. **`draw_util` + `render_target` + the backend resolve path are one
coupled unit and must be ported together** — the base-layer port unblocks the *compile* of
draw.cpp itself, but the shared resolve structs bind it to the backends.

**Implication for sequencing:** a full Canary GPU port should first **port/refresh the base
support layer** (base math additions, `swcache` prefetch + RingBuffer extensions, a
LoggerBatch equivalent, and either upgrade glslang or keep the inert `spv::` shim), *then*
the GPU subsystems merge cleanly. Piecemeal GPU-only merges keep hitting these floors and
must stub/defer the dependent Canary features. The clean wins so far are exactly the files
that touch none of these (DXBC shader path, leaf translators, ucode, draw_extent_estimator).

## SPIRV cluster — HARD-BLOCKED on glslang 11.6.0+ (finding from the overhaul attempt)

A full THEIRS merge of the SPIRV cluster was landed unverified, then a compile-fix
pass was attempted. It revealed the **decisive blocker**: Canary's SPIRV code targets
**glslang 11.6.0+**, and ReXGlue is on an older glslang. Canary's own
`spirv_builder.h` comments say so, and it uses that newer API directly:
- `spv::Builder::createBranch(true, block)` — 2-arg; ReXGlue's glslang takes 1 arg.
- `spv::Builder::makeFunctionEntry(..., spv::LinkageType::Max, ...)` — `LinkageType`
  doesn't exist in ReXGlue's glslang.
- "glslang 11.6.0+ uses internal accessChain state instead of parameters" —
  `createAccessChain` signature differs.

ReXGlue's **existing** `spirv_builder` already works against its old glslang; Canary's
is a shim *for the new one*. So the SPIRV path cannot be ported by rex-ifying or
re-merging headers — it needs the **glslang submodule upgraded to 11.6.0+** first
(which also removes the need for the inert `spirv_compatibility.h` shim), or Canary's
`spirv_builder` rewritten against the old glslang API. This is a prerequisite, not a
per-file fix.

The overhaul also confirmed two lesser issues (once glslang is handled): resolving
headers to THEIRS **duplicates relocated members** (needs a proper union merge of
`spirv_translator.h`), and `SystemConstants` gains members the 4 backend populators
must set (`d3d12`/`vulkan` `pipeline_cache.cpp` + `command_processor.cpp`).

**Outcome:** the unverified overhaul (`896917d`) was reverted; the SPIRV cluster is
back at its built-green pre-overhaul state. DXBC path + leaf files remain on Canary.

### glslang upgrade — scoped (the real number is 16.0.0, not "11.6.0+")

Canary's `spirv_builder.h` comment says "glslang 11.6.0+", but that understates it.
Canary pins glslang at commit `a57276bf` = **glslang 16.0.0 (2025-09)**; ReXGlue's
submodule is at ~**11.0.0 (2020)** — a **5-year, 5-major-version jump**. Tested empirically:
- glslang **11.13.0** configures + builds with ReXGlue's CMake, but still lacks
  `SPIRV/spirv.hpp11`, `spvUtil.h`, and `spv::LinkageType::Max` — so it does NOT satisfy Canary.
- glslang **16.0.0** (Canary's pin) fails to configure with ReXGlue's CMake immediately:
  `install TARGETS given target "OGLCompiler" which does not exist` — glslang removed the
  OGLCompiler/HLSL sub-libraries and restructured targets across 11->16.

**Scope of the real upgrade** (all required together; the bump alone breaks ReXGlue's
old-glslang `spirv_builder`):
1. Bump `thirdparty/glslang` submodule 11.0 -> 16.0.0 (commit `a57276bf`).
2. Rework CMake integration in `thirdparty/CMakeLists.txt` + `cmake/rexglue_install.cmake`
   for glslang 16's target layout (drop OGLCompiler/HLSL refs, fix target names/aliases).
3. Likely bump `thirdparty/spirv-headers` (needs scoped-enum `spirv.hpp11`) and possibly
   `spirv-tools`, matched to glslang 16.
4. Land Canary's `spirv_builder.{h,cpp}` (the wrapper written for glslang 16) + the real
   `spirv_compatibility.h` macro shim (replacing the inert stub).
5. Land Canary's SPIRV translators (already staged in overhaul `896917d`).
6. Fix `spirv_translator.h` duplicate members (proper union merge, not THEIRS).
7. Reconcile `SystemConstants` -> the 4 backend populators.
Backend inline SPIR-V (`vulkan/render_target_cache.cpp`) is largely insulated by Canary's
`SpirvBuilder` wrapper (old-style calls, wrapper adapts), so it needs little direct change.

This is a discrete infrastructure project, not a per-file port. It is the single unlock for
the entire SPIRV shader path. Recommend doing it as a dedicated effort with a Windows build
available (d3d12 shader path can't be verified on macOS).

### glslang 16 upgrade — EXECUTED (keystone done; vulkan-backend reconciliation remains)

The upgrade is landed and validated on macOS:
- `thirdparty/glslang` bumped 11.0 -> **16.0.0** (`a57276bf`). **Configures + builds** with
  ReXGlue's toolchain and current spirv-headers/spirv-tools (no dep bump needed — glslang 16
  bundles `SPIRV/spirv.hpp11` + `spvUtil.h` + `LinkageType`).
- CMake fix: dropped the removed `OGLCompiler` target from `cmake/rexglue_install.cmake` +
  `src/graphics/CMakeLists.txt`. That one change was sufficient to configure.
- Canary's `spirv_builder.{h,cpp}`, real `spirv_compatibility.h` macro shim, and SPIRV
  translators landed on top. **The glslang-API errors are gone** (LinkageType, 2-arg
  createBranch, spirv.hpp11). Duplicate-member merge artifacts fixed by using **clean
  rexform'd headers** (not THEIRS merges). `rex/ui/vulkan/vulkan_*` -> `rex/ui/vulkan/*`
  de-prefix fixed. `xe::bit_scan_forward` -> `rex::`.
- **The SPIRV translators + shader headers now compile on glslang 16.**

**Remaining (WIP, branch does NOT build): `SystemConstants` -> vulkan backend port.**
This is a **feature-level port, not a rename map** (verified against Canary's own backend):
- Canary **restructured** vertex-index handling: dropped `vertex_index_min/max/reset` from
  SystemConstants in favor of `vertex_index_load_address` + `vertex_index_endian`. ReXGlue's
  backend must adopt Canary's population approach, not remap fields.
- Canary **removed** `tessellation_factor_range_*`, `line_loop_closing_index`, and
  `compute_memexport_vertex_count` from SystemConstants (its backend sets them 0 times) --
  those features moved/changed; the ReXGlue backend code that computes+sets them is obsolete.
- `textures_resolution_scaled` -> `textures_resolved` (rename); `zpd_fsi_counter_index` added.
- Because SystemConstants is a **CPU<->GPU contract** (shaders read it by layout), stubbing
  the backend to compile would silently break vertex processing -- NOT done. Correct fix is
  to port Canary's `vulkan/pipeline_cache.cc` + `vulkan/command_processor.cc` constant
  population, which is coupled with the full vulkan-backend port + the PM4 changes already on
  `vulkan/command_processor.cpp`, and needs a Windows build for the d3d12 half.
- Mechanical part only: the scoped `spv::ExecutionMode*` / `Modification::DepthStencilMode`
  enumerator errors are covered by `#include`ing `spirv_compatibility.h` (it maps them).

**Branch state:** tip (`c2460cc` + docs) carries the glslang-16 keystone but does not build.
To get a working branch immediately, `git revert` the glslang/SPIRV commits (they stay in
history for resumption). To finish the SPIRV path, do the vulkan-backend port as its own unit.

## PM4 landing progress

**Base PM4 mixin is wired and builds green (compile+link) on core + Vulkan (macOS,
Debug/RelWithDebInfo/Release).** The base `CommandProcessor` now injects
`pm4_command_processor_declare.h` into its class body and compiles
`pm4_command_processor_implement.h` (Canary's shared PM4 dispatch) with the member
`RingBuffer reader_;` model, replacing the ~1073 lines of master-style handlers.

What landed:
- `gpu_attributes.h` — `XE_*` attribute macros + Xenia log-macro aliases (XELOGE→REXGPU_ERROR…).
- `pm4_command_processor_{declare,implement}.h` in `include/rex/graphics/`, ReXGlue-adapted.
- `command_processor.{h,cpp}` — declare include, `reader_` member, implement include,
  `WriteOneRegisterFromRing` helper.
- Vulkan + D3D12 `EVENT_WRITE_ZPD` overrides converted to the member-reader signature.

Design decision — **base-only adoption**: calls to backend-overridden virtuals
(`IssueDraw/IssueSwap/LoadShader/OnPrimaryBufferEnd/WriteRegister/EVENT_WRITE_ZPD`) are
**unqualified** so the base handlers dispatch virtually to the real backend method.
Correct without per-backend monomorphization; the `COMMAND_PROCESSOR::` devirtualization
is the deferred perf win.

Intentionally dropped in the initial port (documented in the headers):
- PM4 structured disassembly (`DisassembleCurrentPacket`) — needs a LoggerBatch API ReXGlue lacks.
- `BeginPrefetchedRead` swcache hints — perf-only.
- Canary ZPD occlusion-query subsystem — ReXGlue's fake-sample fallback preserved instead.
- MEM_WRITE writeback-region address remap (`XE_GPU_REG_WRITEBACK_*`).

**NOT yet verified / remaining:**
- **Runtime correctness is unverified** — compile+link only. The member-reader lifecycle and
  interrupt/swap paths need GPU trace-golden diffs against a few titles before this is trusted.
- **D3D12 not compiled here** (backend off on macOS); the `EVENT_WRITE_ZPD` conversion is
  mechanical but must be built on Windows.
- **Per-backend monomorphization** (OVERRIDING_BASE_CMDPROCESSOR + implement.h per backend)
  deferred — restores the hot-loop devirtualization.
- Restore prefetch / structured disasm / ZPD subsystem as follow-ups.
